content.text: Channeling the power of vile otherworldly entities into your body, you take a new grotesque form, allowing you to wade into the battlefield while spreading pain and terror in your wake. You transform yourself into a Large aberration. You must have enough space to expand into, or the spell is lost. When you Cast this Spell, choose chuul, gogiteth, gug, or ofalth. While in this form, you gain the aberration trait. You can Dismiss the spell.
You gain the following statistics and abilities regardless of which battle form you choose:
AC = 18 + your level. Ignore your armor's check penalty and Speed reduction.

One or more unarmed melee attacks specific to the battle form you choose, which are the only attacks you can Strike with. You're trained with them. Your attack modifier is +18, and your damage bonus is +8. These attacks are Strength based (for the purpose of the enfeebled condition, for example). If your unarmed attack modifier is higher, you can use it instead.
Athletics modifier of +20, unless your own modifier is higher.
You also gain specific abilities based on the type of aberration you choose:
2d8 bludgeoning, and after a successful Strike, you can spend an action to attempt to Grab the target.
2d10 piercing, and after a successful Strike, you can spend an action to attempt to Grab the target
your multiple joints allow you to fit through tight spaces as if you were a Medium creature.
+2 circumstance bonus on saves against disease and poison

Your battle form is Huge, and the reach of your attacks increases by 5 feet. You must have space to expand, or the spell is lost. You instead gain AC = 21 + your level, 26 temporary Hit Points, attack modifier +22, damage bonus +13, and Athletics +23.

You choose a location within range that you can see and haphazardly catapult yourself and the target through space, attempting to violate one of the cardinal laws of teleportation by intertwining your own magical signature with that of the target creature as if you both were a single being. The target must attempt a Fortitude save.
The target is unaffected, but you're instantly transported to the chosen space.
You and a piece of the target are transported to the chosen location, fused together. The target becomes
, and you gain 20 temporary Hit Points until the end of your next turn.

You and the target creature vanish from your current locations and reappear in the chosen space fused together until the end of your next turn. While fused together, you also gain the following effects.
You gain 40 temporary Hit Points that last for the duration of the spell.
You gain all Speeds possessed by the target, unless you already have a higher Speed of that kind.
You gain all special senses possessed by the target.

Your reach increases by 5 feet. While fused, the target creature doesn't occupy space, is unable to act, and can't be targeted or affected by attacks or other effects. The target does remain aware of its environment and everything transpiring around it. At the end of your next turn, the target separates from you in an adjacent space. Both you and the target return to your original forms.
As failure, except the target also becomes

Invoking the celestial realms, you transform into a Medium angel battle form. When you Cast this Spell, choose balisse, choral, kuribu, or tennin. The battle form is Small if you choose choral or kuribu. While in this form, you gain the angel, celestial, and holy traits. You have hands in this battle form and can use manipulate actions. You can Dismiss the spell.
You gain the following statistics and abilities regardless of the form that you choose:
AC = 22 + your level. Ignore your armor's check penalty and Speed reduction. 40 temporary Hit Points and weakness 10 to unholy.

One or more attacks specific to the battle form you choose, which are the only attacks you can Strike with. You're trained with them. Your attack modifier is +25, and your damage bonus is +12. Melee attacks are Strength based (for the purpose of the enfeebled condition, for example), and ranged attacks are Dexterity based. If your attack modifier is higher for the given unarmed attack or weapon, you can use it instead.
Athletics modifier of +25, unless your own modifier is higher.
You also gain specific abilities based on the type of angel you choose:
Speed 30 feet, fly 40 feet; Perception modifier of +26 to detect lies and illusions unless your own modifier is higher
Speed 30 feet, fly 40 feet; +1 status bonus to AC and saves against auditory and sonic
for 1 round on a critical hit.
Speed 25 feet, fly 40 feet; resistance 10 to electricity and fire
composite shortbow (deadly 2d10, holy, magical, propulsive, range increment 60 feet),
Speed 30 feet, fly 60 feet; can Step into difficult terrain and use land and fly Speeds to Step

Your battle form is Large if you choose balisse or tennin. You must have space to expand into, or the spell is lost. You instead gain AC = 22 + your level, 60 temporary Hit Points, weakness 15 to unholy, attack modifier +30, damage bonus +20, and Athletics +33.

You summon tiny, ordinary animals from the environment, such as insects, birds, or fish, to quickly lash out at nearby foes. The animals swarm around the creatures in the area, dealing each of them 3d4 piercing damage with a basic Reflex save.
You implant a thought in your target's mind that resembles an authority figure in their life, influencing how they feel about you. The target attempts a Will save.

The target harbors some small resentment toward the authority figure you invoked. The target takes a –1 status penalty to saves against your emotion effects, but can attempt another Will save at the end of each of its turns, ending the spell's effect on a success.
The target believes the resemblance and is susceptible to your influence, taking a –1 status penalty to saves against your emotion effects.
As failure, except the status penalty is –2.
You can target up to 4 creatures.

Your magic quickly flows over an area to help you count and catalog. Name a particular type of object you're looking for within the area. You gain an instant estimate of the quantity of the chosen objects that are clearly visible within the target area. The number is rounded to the largest digit. For example, you could look at a pile of 180 copper coins, and you would learn that it held about 200 coins, but you couldn't determine there were exactly 180 coins.

The type of object you name can be as specific or general as you like—"dented copper coins" is as viable as "coins"—but the distinguishing features must be obvious at a glance, and the spell is fooled by objects disguised as other objects.

You touch your finger to a blank surface and create an image of a person, place, or object. This image appears instantly in the style of a pastel-hued oil painting and disappears cleanly once the spell ends. The portrait is the size of one average sketchbook page and must represent a subject the caster has seen in person or has studied extensively.

You summon a tumultuous cloud of ash and smoke. The cloud is difficult terrain for flying creatures, and creatures in the cloud can't detect anything using their sense of smell. Creatures that start their turn within the cloud take 2d4 fire damage as their lungs fill with the hot, acrid smoke, with a Fortitude save.
The target takes full damage and is
The target takes double damage and is

You cloak the targets in an illusion, shaping their clothing and worn items into ones suitable for a particular occasion. You visualize the occasion, and the spell creates illusory attire customized to each target. For instance, if you visualized a noble ball, armor would appear to be fine clothing. This doesn't change identifying details of the targets' appearances other than their clothes.
Any creature that touches the attire, uses the Seek action to examine it, or otherwise interacts with it can attempt to disbelieve your illusion.
You can target up to 20 creatures.
You can target up to 100 creatures.

With but a touch, a mystical force sends a foe rocketing backward. The target creature must attempt a Fortitude save. If the creature's movement causes it to hit a firm surface, such as a wall, it takes
damage. A creature knocked off a ledge or the like can Grab an Edge to avoid falling.
The creature is pushed 5 feet away from you.
The creature is pushed 15 feet away from you.
The creature is pushed 30 feet away from you.

You turn one of your thralls into a conduit to bind the spirit of a hero into your body. Destroy the target thrall and gain a +1 status bonus to attack rolls and saving throws. Additionally, whenever you critically hit a creature with a Strike, you can create a thrall in a space adjacent to the target of the Strike, as your heroic attack inspires other spirits to join you on the battlefield.

You entwine magic with your voice, causing your taunts and jibes to physically harm your enemies. You can attack with your words once when you finish Casting the Spell, and can repeat the attack once on each of your subsequent turns by taking a single action, which has the attack, concentrate, and linguistic traits. After your third attack total, the spell ends.
When you attack with biting words, make a ranged spell attack roll against a creature within 30 feet, dealing 2d6 sonic damage if you hit (or double damage on a critical hit).

Superheated air collects under you, buoying you high into the sky before you plummet back down in a fiery comet. You Fly 15 feet straight up into the air, then Fly in a straight line to an empty space of your choice on the ground within 60 feet. When you land, blistering air blasts out from you, dealing 3d4 bludgeoning damage and 3d6 fire damage (basic Reflex save) to all creatures in a 10-foot emanation.
The damage increases by 1d4 bludgeoning and 1d6 fire.
A thin crack rips through the earth, erupting with magma, then swiftly seals up. Each creature along the line and on solid ground takes 4d6 bludgeoning damage and 6d6 fire damage with a Reflex save.
The creature takes full damage, and it falls
The creature takes double damage, and it falls prone.
The damage increases by 1d6 bludgeoning and 1d6 fire.

Channeling forth the power to persevere in the face of adversity. Choose one saving throw: Fortitude, Reflex, or Will. The target gains a +4 status bonus to that saving throw for 1 round. The potency and number of targets of this blessing depend on how many actions you spend when Casting the Spell.
The spell targets you or one willing ally within range.

The spell targets you or one willing ally within range. If you choose Fortitude, the target gains resistance 15 to poison. If you choose Reflex, the target gains a +15-foot status bonus to its Speeds. If you choose Will, the target gains resistance 15 to mental damage.
The spell targets you and all willing allies within 30 feet.
You pray for a small blessing to keep your target safe. The target gains fast healing 3.

You propel yourself through the fabric of space to deal a blow carrying the momentum of your teleportation. You teleport to an empty space adjacent to a creature you can see within range, then make a Strike against the creature with a weapon you're wielding. The Strike deals damage, plus an additional 2d8 force damage, depending on the result of your Strike.

Double damage, plus after the Strike, you can teleport the target into an empty space up to 5 feet away from its current position. The new space must be on the ground if it started on the ground, in the air if it was flying, and so on.
The Strike deals no damage, but the target takes 1d8 force damage.
The Strike deals no damage, and you take 1d8 force damage.
The spell's range increases by 60 feet, and any force damage the spell deals is increased by 1d8.
With a wave of your arm, you launch a handful of sharp crimson seeds that bury themselves in the target's flesh. The target takes 3d8 piercing damage with a Fortitude save.
The target takes half the piercing damage.
The target takes full piercing damage and becomes afflicted with draining growth at stage 1.
The target takes double the piercing damage and becomes afflicted with draining growth at stage 2.
(disease) The target can't reduce their drained condition while afflicted by draining growth

damage as a single chestnut tree begins to grow out of the creature's body. The target can't end this bleed damage until the tree is destroyed. The tree has AC 10 and 40 Hit Points, and it's immune to critical hits and precision damage. Once the tree is destroyed, return to stage 2.

You pull blood and other fluid from a thrall before embedding it into another creature. You then slowly and painfully begin to extract that blood from the creature. A creature within 15 feet of the target thrall becomes filled with blood. The thrall is destroyed, and the creature must attempt a Fortitude saving throw.
The target loses any immunity to bleed and is considered to be a creature with blood for the purposes of effects and requirements. The creature takes (@item.rank)[bleed] damage.
As success, but the persistent bleed damage is (@item.rank)d6[bleed].
As success, but the persistent bleed damage is (@item.rank*2)d6[bleed].
The persistent bleed damage increases by 1 on a success, 1d6 on a failure, and 2d6 on a critical failure.
You chill the blood in the target's veins. The target takes 1d6 persistent cold damage with a Fortitude save.
The target takes half the persistent cold damage.
The target takes the full persistent cold damage and is
The target takes double the persistent cold damage and is slowed 1 until the persistent cold damage ends.
Increase the persistent cold damage by 1d6.
You inflict a curse upon the target that causes any wound to gush blood. The target must attempt a Fortitude save.

For 1 minute, the first time each round that the target would take at least 10 piercing or slashing damage from a single Strike, the strike deals an additional (floor(@item.rank/2))d6[piercing] or (floor(@item.rank/2))d6[slashing] damage of the same type.
As success, but the Strike also deals an additional (floor(@item.rank/2))d6[bleed] damage.
The additional damage increases by 1d6, and the persistent bleed damage increases by 1d6.

You conjure forth stationary tentacles formed from pure, partially hardened blood. You create up to 3 Medium thralls shaped like bloody tendrils in range. These tendrils are immune to physical damage and can't move. The tendril's Strike has a reach of 10 feet. Whenever an enemy ends it turn within the reach of one or more tendrils, the tendril lashes out at them, dealing 1d12 bludgeoning damage with a basic Reflex save.
The number of thralls this spell can create increases by 1, and the damage increases by 1d12.

By spilling the blood of a thrall, you grow a large field of bloody roses that feeds on the life force of those around it and uses it to create thralls that do your bidding. This field appears in a 20-foot burst centered on a corner in the target thrall's space, and that thrall is destroyed. A creature that enters or starts its turn in the area takes 10 persistent bleed damage from the rose's thorns. You can Dismiss this spell.
If a bleeding creature ends its turn in the area, it must attempt a Fortitude saving throw.
The creature is drained 1, and a single thrall is created in an unoccupied space adjacent to the field.
, and 2 thralls are created in unoccupied spaces adjacent to the field.
The persistent bleed damage increases by 2.

A tiny, bone-white moth emerges from your open mouth. It shakes itself off, spreads its wings, and flies toward your foe, brushing its wings against their exposed skin. The moth carries a disease that causes a victim's bones to quickly grow soft and eventually melt. The target must attempt a Fortitude save.
The moth only briefly brushes its wings against the target. The target is
The moth lands on the target, kissing the spot with its fluttering. The target is afflicted with the bone moth's kiss at stage 1.
The moth lands on an open wound, targeting it with its kiss. The target is afflicted with the bone moth's kiss at stage 2.
and can't recover from the drained condition until the disease is cured (1 day)

You create an expendable shield of rough, raw bone in a free hand that can easily be replaced over and over again. When you Cast the Spell or the first time each round you Sustain this spell on subsequent rounds, you can Raise this Shield, granting you a +2 circumstance bonus to AC. While this spell is in effect, you gain the Shield Block reaction, but only with the bone shield. The bone shield has Hardness 3 and 1 HP (with no Broken Threshold). This shield also gains a +2 circumstance bonus to its Hardness against attacks that deal piercing or slashing damage. If the shield is destroyed, it's recreated already raised in a free hand when you Sustain the Spell.

You shape a thrall into a spear of jagged bone. Destroy the target thrall, and each creature in a 15-foot line originating from the thrall's former space takes 2d6 piercing damage with a basic Reflex save.

You fire a torrent of jagged bone shards from your hands that rips through the fleshy bodies of your enemies. The spray deals 2d10 piercing damage and 1 persistent bleed damage to all creatures in the area, with a basic Reflex save.
The piercing damage increases by 1d10, and the persistent bleed damage increases by 1.

You shatter the skeleton of a thrall, creating a volley of teeth, vertebrae, and phalanges. Destroy the target thrall, and each creature in a 30-foot cone originating from the thrall's former space takes 2d10 piercing damage with a basic Reflex save. You can destroy a second thrall in the cone's area to cover you and any allies in the area in bone armor. If you do, you and affected allies take no damage from this spell and gain a +1 status bonus to AC until the start of your next turn.

You amplify the already intense cracking noise of your gunshot to spread terror through the ranks of your foes. Make a ranged firearm Strike. Regardless of the result, each enemy in a 20-foot emanation around you must succeed at a Will save against your spell DC or be

You focus deeply on the link between you and your eidolon and boost the power of your eidolon's attacks. Your eidolon gains a +2 status bonus to damage rolls with their unarmed attacks. If your eidolon's Strikes deal more than one weapon damage die, the status bonus increases to 2 per weapon damage die, to a maximum of +8 with four weapon damage dice.
Your eidolon can benefit from either
, but not both; if you cast one of these spells during the other's duration, the newer spell replaces the older one.

You create a shimmering extradimensional space accessible from the target's mouth. The space can hold objects and equipment, up to a total of 10 Bulk. This extradimensional storage doesn't hamper the target's ability to eat, drink, speak (if applicable), or otherwise act, as it only opens and closes when the target chooses.

The target can Interact to swallow an object of up to 1 Bulk, which doesn't harm the object or the target. If the extradimensional space is full, the target can't add any more objects until first removing one or more stored objects. Organic matter and living creatures can't be stored in this space. The extradimensional storage is obvious to any creature who looks into the target's mouth, as the entryway shimmers slightly, though this doesn't clearly reveal the contents inside.

The target can Interact to spit out a single object of their choice, causing the object to fall to the ground in the target's space. The target can Interact three times in a row to spit out the entire contents of the extradimensional storage; the target doesn't have to take these actions all in the same turn, but if they take any other actions in between, the target has to start over. The items eject into the target's space, possibly spilling out into adjacent spaces if there's too much to fit.
When the spell ends or the target falls
, the contents of the extradimensional storage are disgorged in a riotous spew, landing in the nearest unoccupied space, a bit wet but otherwise unharmed.

You protect your target from going astray in hostile territory by tracking where they've already been, helping the target deduce where they still need to go. The target leaves a glittering trail behind them that lasts for the spell's duration. This trail doesn't denote the direction or the order of its path—it merely indicates where the target has moved during the spell's duration.
The duration increases to last until your next daily preparations.

You summon a bridge formed from grave dirt and tombstones that allow thralls to move with great speed. The 10-foot-wide span must start at the ground on a point within range, and it extends as a horizontal plane, either in a straight line or at any angle up to 45 degrees upward or downward, for up to 120 feet. This bridge has AC 10, Hardness 30, and 40 Hit Points. A thrall on or adjacent to the bridge can move to any location on the bridge when you command it to Stride. You can Dismiss the spell.
The length of the bridge increases by 20 feet, its Hit Points increase by 20, and you can increase the width of the span by up to an additional 5 feet.

An intangible hollow tree grows to towering height, radiating a fiery passion and fascinating viewers. The base of the tree takes up a single square and grows 100 feet upward, while its branches extend outward 30 feet, forming the spell's cylindrical area. The tree then blossoms, growing delicate white flowers that burn with white-hot fire. As the tree's branches gently rustle in the wind, flower petals drift to the ground in a shower of flame. Any creature that ends its turn under the tree's branches takes 6d6 fire damage from the burning petals. Any enemy that can see the tree, even if the enemy is outside the spell's area, must attempt a Will save. This is an emotion, mental, and visual effect. Creatures
with the tree must use at least one of their actions on each of their turns to move toward the tree.
The creature is unaffected and is temporarily immune for 24 hours.
The creature is unaffected, but it must attempt a new save at the end of its turn if it can still see the tree.
with the tree until the end of its next turn. If it can still see the tree at the end of its turn, it must attempt a new save.

The creature is fascinated with the tree until the spell ends. The tree's fire damage doesn't end the fascination, but other hostile actions end it as normal. If the fascination ends, the creature must attempt a new save at the end of its turn if it can still see the tree.

The target's feet glow with a magical flame that lingers and grows on the ground where they walk, creating a line of blazing fire as they move. The first time the target Strides during the spell's duration, they leave behind a trail made of magical fire that fills up each space they occupied during that Stride. This fire is 5 feet high. Creatures on either side of the trail are
from creatures on the opposite side. Any creature that enters or starts its turn in the trail's area takes 2d10 fire damage.

You transform a thrall into fine dust particles that invade a creature's body and begin transforming their body into a statue made of pure enhanced bone. Destroy a thrall within range, and choose a living or undead creature within 60 feet of where the thrall was. The creature begins solidifying into pure bone depending on its Fortitude save. Creatures already made purely of bone, such as skeletons, are immune to this spell. An incorporeal creature slowed by this spell loses the incorporeal trait and all associated resistances for the duration of the spell.
and has weakness 5 to bludgeoning for 1 round.
The creature is slowed 1 and has weakness 10 to bludgeoning for as long as it's slowed. The creature must attempt an additional

save at the end of each of its turns; this ongoing save has the incapacitation trait. On a failed save, the slowed condition increases by 1 (or 2 on a critical failure) as bone growths creep across the creature's body. A successful save reduces the slowed condition by 1.
When a creature becomes fully unable to act due to the slowed condition from
, the spell then ends, leaving the creature
permanently as it becomes a bony statue. The spell also ends if the slowed condition is removed, which causes the bone to break off harmlessly.
As failure, but the target is initially

You conjure a horrific cloud of tiny dancing bone shards that collapses like a torrent of rain upon those unfortunate enough to be nearby. Creatures in the area take 10d4 piercing damage and 5 persistent bleed damage (basic Reflex save).
The piercing damage increases by 2d4, and the persistent bleed damage increases by 1.

Legends say Aroden and Arazni called upon the Boundless Sea itself to defeat the fiery lizard Cuetzmonquali and the Army of Fire. Using yourself as the planar key, you blow the conch to call forth a boundless sea and its inhabitants to aid you. Water falls as a torrential shower, making the area of the spell difficult terrain for all enemies. You and all allies within the area gain resistance 15 to fire and are
. Countless sea creatures swim through the sky and attack your foes. An enemy that ends its turn within the area takes 7d4 piercing and 7d4 bludgeoning damage (basic Reflex save).

spell without expending a spell slot. The animal you summon must have the amphibious or aquatic trait and gains a fly Speed equal to its swim Speed. You can Sustain any number of animals created this way whenever you Sustain this spell.

You become closely aligned with elemental water and constantly feel sluggish while away from it. You take a –5-foot status penalty to your land Speed that's suppressed when you're within 1 mile of an ocean or a portal to the Plane of Water. You heal the mark if you take damage from dragon breath from three different dragons with the primal or water trait.
The bludgeoning and piercing damage both increase by 1d4. The rank of the
a conch from the Plane of Water worth 1,000 gp × the spell's rank

You release a wave of temporal energy that sends creatures violently tumbling through time, scarring their thoughts with the information flowing around them. Although the journey can feel like it lasts for minutes or even days, the targets reappear instantly. Witnessing this chaotic flow of time and being bashed against objects from the past and future deals 5d8 mental damage and 5d6 bludgeoning damage to creatures in the area, with a Fortitude save. A creature that falls into time disappears until the end of your turn. It then reappears in the same space it left; if that space is occupied, it appears in the nearest empty space, chosen by the GM. Creatures that are immune to mental effects can still be affected by this spell but take no mental damage.
The creature falls into time. When it returns, it takes half damage.
The creature falls into time. When it returns, it takes full damage and is
The creature falls into time. When it returns, it takes double damage and is

The target can change the direction gravity pulls them after they touch a surface with their feet. The target can walk on vertical surfaces or upside down as though gravity was pulling them toward the surface. In addition, the target gains a +1 status bonus to their saving throws and Fortitude DC against forced movement. When the spell ends, the target is affected by gravity as normal and might fall if not on the floor.

Conjuring a quill of magical flame, you take an object and write a message onto it that disappears to the naked eye almost as soon as you finish writing it. If this message is written onto an object that can't withstand a burning fire, such as paper or leather, then the object is destroyed while you're writing it. If the inscribed object is thrust into a roaring fire, the writing on it is revealed for 1 minute before fading. The writing can be revealed this way any number of times, and it's erased only if it's counteracted by an effect similar to dispel magic or when the duration ends. Even if the object is destroyed, pieces of the message exist on its various parts. For example, if the object was turned to dust and recreated via remake, the message would remain intact.
The duration increases to a year and a day.

Winning magical combat often requires exploiting weakness. You evoke a circle of floating inscriptions that creates and amplifies energy-based weaknesses on creatures inside the circle. Choose one type of damage from the following list: acid, cold, electricity, fire, force, or sonic. When you Cast the Spell and the first time you Sustain it each turn, each creature in the area must attempt a Fortitude saving throw.
The creature gains weakness 1 to the chosen damage type for 1 round.
As success, except the weakness is doubled.

for 1 round or until they Escape.
The weakness gained on a success increases by 1.

By burning threads of fate around a target and then retying them to yourself instead, you temporarily draw their curse to you, offering them brief succor from the worst of its effects. Choose a curse affecting the target that you don't already have. For 5 minutes, you're affected by the curse (at the same stage as the target, and it can't be changed, if applicable), and the target isn't. If the curse's duration ends before claim curse would, it ends as normal; otherwise, when the spell's duration ends the curse's effects return to the target as normal.
You create a duplicate of your companion that fights alongside its twin, mirroring the original's actions. The duplicate appears adjacent to your companion and has the same statistics.

Each time you Command your companion, both your companion and its duplicate gain 2 actions. The duplicate always acts immediately after your companion and must use identical actions to the ones your companion used, in exactly the same order. However, it can use the actions differently, such as Striding to a different position or selecting a different target for a Strike. If the duplicate is unable to mimic an action, it performs the action without result, and the action is wasted. The duplicate can't use any actions that can be used only a limited number of times per day.
The duplicate isn't truly alive and can't be healed in any way. If the duplicate ever reaches 0 Hit Points, it's instantly destroyed, and clone companion ends immediately.

Wreathed in elemental power, you launch yourself toward a target to deliver a mighty blow. You Fly up to 120 feet in a straight line to an empty space adjacent to the target creature and make a melee spell attack. This movement doesn't trigger reactions, and you can fly through other creatures as part of this movement. If you began this movement at a higher elevation than your target, it's
When you Cast this Spell, choose one of the elemental effects below. The spell gains the traits listed, and the melee spell attack gains the chosen elemental effect.

for 1 round. On a critical hit, the target takes double damage.

for 1 minute. On a critical hit, the target takes double damage. The target can Interact to remove the splinters and end the clumsy condition inflicted by this spell.

The shadow of your companion joins in the fight. The first time your companion Strikes each round, their shadow can also make an unarmed Strike against a different creature within range using the same multiple attack penalty as the original attack. The shadow's Strike deals void damage instead of any other damage type the Strike would normally do. Both attacks contribute to your companion's multiple attack penalty as normal.
You conjure forth a humongous thrall consisting solely of undead severed limbs. You create a Huge thrall within range. This thrall has 40 Hit Points and a Speed of 25 feet.

The thrall's Hit Points increase by 10.

The resistance from this spell is cumulative with that of
. If you're in Arcane Cascade stance when the duration of
expires, the spell's duration extends until Arcane Cascade ends.

Razor sharp coral erupts from the ground, transforming the landscape into a dangerous coral reef. You can create a third nonoverlapping burst if the centers of all three bursts are underwater. Creatures in the area when the spell is cast take 6d6 piercing damage and must attempt a basic Reflex save. A creature that critically fails its saving throw also takes
The area becomes difficult terrain and hazardous terrain. A creature that moves through the area takes (floor(@item.rank/2)+1)[piercing] damage for every square of that area it moves into.
The initial piercing damage increases by 3d6, and the hazardous terrain damage increases by 1.

You conjure three deadly clusters of flesh-devouring fungi. Whenever a creature starts its turn in one of the clusters or the first time a creature enters a cluster each round, it takes 3d4 poison damage with a Fortitude save as poisonous spores fill the air. Corpses within a cluster rapidly decompose.
